answer.rationale: Writes are at daily peak and the must-not-revert security patch rules out a release rollback; failover risks a write-availability cliff while writes are heavy and non-revertible state on the new build is still inbound, so a targeted, observable write-path capacity bump — anchored in the day‑47 lesson that provisioning headroom absorbed the peak with flat queues — gives a reversible way to lower p99 without touching the patch or moving traffic. A small guarded step is preferred over a single large blast, since the rollback path on a capacity move is still open and the situation is fluid. No memory needs re-opening today: the b3 record aligns cleanly with the moment and the plan.
